summary: Amador County lookout tower erected by the State in 1930 near Pine Grove; NHLR-registered 2019; a May 2020 visit report says Cal Fire V.I.P. staffing was planned from June 1, 2020.

facts.design: Aermotor Company tower erected by the State in 1930; BC-201 lookout residence built under the ECW program; office, water tower and garage that may date from 1932

access.note: Locked gate blocks vehicles up to the tower except Cal Fire, Cal Fire V.I.P. and repeater vault access; per the May 14, 2020 visit report the tower itself is not open to the average visitor

visit.trail_note: Parking at the intersection of Mount Zion Rd. and Lookout Rd.; trails and a gravel road lead near the tower; people could walk up to the tower fence as of May 2020

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An April 1930 notice expected a Sunday dedication; a June 3, 1930 report describes a Friday afternoon dedication. Not resolved; the story reports the two accounts without choosing.
A 1928 report places the station near Pine Grove and a March 1930 item says near Jackson. Both are in Amador County; the story uses Pine Grove and mentions the other.
The Register says a tree lookout may have existed before 1930; the 1927 and 1928 newspaper items describe a station being chosen and staffed. The story does not make a claim about a tree lookout.

notes_for_editor: Current staffing and access are only confirmed to May 14, 2020 (visit report). The planned June 1, 2020 start is a plan, not a confirmed fact; the staffing status says so. No rental source was read and no later visit report appears on the NHLR page. The weebly newspaper items end in 1931. The tower's height is a 1929 plan (70 ft) and a 1930 comparison (50 ft taller than the old station), not a measured figure, so no height_m is recorded. No corrections to the brief's record were found. Budget: about three page reads and no web searches used.
